title: Enterprise Client Onboarding and Relationship Management
goal: Successfully onboard a new enterprise client from signed contract through to active account, establishing the ongoing relationship management rhythm that sustains and grows the account
summary: A B2B sales CRM workflow covering the critical first 90 days of a new enterprise client relationship — from post-contract kick-off through activation, first renewal signal, and ongoing account health management. Designed for senior sales reps using Salesforce or equivalent CRM.

assumptions: CRM (Salesforce) is the system of record
Sales rep has quota responsibility for the account during onboarding
Implementation is handled by a separate CS/technical team

actors.role: primary account owner and relationship lead

laneContent.description: Deal closes. Sales rep receives handover from deal team and assumes full account ownership
Sales rep creates and populates the client account record in Salesforce: contacts, contract value, renewal date, account tier, and initial health score

channels.name: Salesforce CRM
channels.usageContext: Account record creation and data entry

barriers.description: Deal team often uses different field conventions — data migration from deal records to account records requires manual reconciliation

laneContent.backstage: Sales rep manually reconciles data from deal team handover sheet into Salesforce account record
design-opps: Auto-populate account record from signed contract data

sla.targetDuration: CRM setup within 24h of contract signing
sla.escalation: Flag to sales manager if setup delayed beyond 48 hours

laneContent.description: Sales rep researches client stakeholders, reviews contract commitments, and prepares kick-off agenda in coordination with CS/implementation team

channels.name: Email
channels.usageContext: Coordinating kick-off logistics with client and internal team

barriers.description: Sales rep has deal-level knowledge but limited visibility of day-to-day client contacts who will actually use the product

laneContent.frontstage: Kick-off meeting invitation and pre-read document sent to client
laneContent.backstage: Internal briefing with CS team, review of contract commitments and implementation timeline
design-opps: AI-powered stakeholder mapping from LinkedIn and client public information

laneContent.description: 90-minute session: introductions, review contract scope and success metrics, agree communication cadence, identify internal champions

channels.name: Teams / Zoom
channels.usageContext: Primary kick-off channel for most enterprise clients

channels.name: On-site meeting (strategic accounts)
channels.usageContext: Tier 1 accounts: in-person kick-off at client offices

barriers.description: Client-side stakeholders invited may not be the actual power users — kick-off can become political rather than practical

laneContent.frontstage: Kick-off agenda, success metrics alignment, communication plan
laneContent.backstage: Sales rep takes structured notes in Salesforce; CS lead captures technical requirements
design-opps: Auto-generate stakeholder map from kick-off attendance and roles

significance.description: Sets the tone for the entire relationship — first impressions determine whether the client views this as a transactional or strategic partnership

laneContent.description: Post kick-off review: has sales rep identified economic buyer, champion, and key users? Missing stakeholders = account risk
laneContent.backstage: Sales rep reviews stakeholder map with manager — accounts with unidentified economic buyers are flagged

laneContent.description: CS/technical team leads implementation. Sales rep maintains client relationship, monitors progress, and escalates blockers to CS lead

channels.name: Email
channels.usageContext: Relationship check-ins and escalation comms during implementation

channels.name: Shared Slack channel (enterprise clients)
channels.usageContext: Real-time coordination for Tier 1 enterprise accounts

barriers.description: No clear escalation path when implementation delays risk client satisfaction — CS and sales accountability boundaries are blurry

laneContent.frontstage: Regular implementation status updates, proactive escalation if timeline slips
laneContent.backstage: CS team manages technical delivery; sales rep monitors Salesforce health score and implementation milestone tracking

laneContent.description: Sales rep-led call at 30 days. Goal: early value realisation check, uncover any adoption concerns, reinforce relationship

barriers.description: No product usage data available in CRM — sales rep can't see whether client is actually adopting the product

laneContent.frontstage: Check-in agenda focusing on early value and any concerns
laneContent.backstage: Salesforce health score reviewed pre-call; CS provides adoption metrics if available
design-opps: Real-time product adoption data surfaced in CRM so sales rep can personalise check-in conversation

sla.targetDuration: Check-in within 35 days of contract signing
sla.escalation: Flag to manager if check-in not booked within 30 days

laneContent.description: Based on check-in: is adoption on track? Low adoption triggers an intervention path; healthy adoption moves to 60-day check-in
laneContent.backstage: Sales rep updates Salesforce health score; flags intervention accounts to CS lead

laneContent.description: For low-adoption accounts: CS and sales jointly identify root cause (product fit, onboarding quality, internal champions) and agree an intervention plan

channels.name: Joint CS/Sales call with client champion
channels.usageContext: Adoption intervention — uncover blockers and agree recovery plan

laneContent.frontstage: Structured recovery plan: additional training, configuration changes, or executive escalation
laneContent.backstage: CS reviews product configuration and usage logs; sales rep prepares recovery plan with manager

laneContent.description: Mid-point check. Focus shifts from adoption to value realisation — can client articulate a business outcome from the product?
laneContent.frontstage: Value realisation review, expansion opportunity discussion if appropriate
laneContent.backstage: Sales rep documents case study potential, identifies upsell opportunity signals in Salesforce
design-opps: Value realisation scoring framework that auto-generates ROI evidence for client business case

laneContent.description: Formal quarterly review: achievement against success metrics, roadmap alignment, expansion opportunity, and renewal intent signal

channels.name: On-site QBR (strategic accounts)
channels.usageContext: 90-day Quarterly Business Review for Tier 1 accounts

barriers.description: Client stakeholders for the QBR are often different from day-to-day contacts — building executive access takes deliberate effort

laneContent.frontstage: QBR deck: achievement vs. metrics, roadmap, next 90-day plan
laneContent.backstage: Sales rep prepares QBR with CS input; manager reviews expansion opportunity before call
design-opps: Auto-generated QBR deck from Salesforce metrics and product usage data

significance.description: First formal review — sets the expectation for ongoing executive engagement and surfaces early renewal intent

laneContent.description: Post-QBR: is renewal likely (green), at risk (amber), or unlikely (red)? Determines account management intensity for next quarter
laneContent.backstage: Sales rep updates renewal forecast in Salesforce; red accounts escalated to manager

laneContent.description: Regular check-ins, expansion conversations, and account health monitoring through the contract term
laneContent.frontstage: Proactive updates, peer benchmarking, early access to new features
laneContent.backstage: Salesforce health score monitoring, expansion pipeline tracking

laneContent.description: Client is actively engaged, adoption healthy, renewal intent positive. Account transitions to standard annual cycle.

paths.name: Healthy onboarding — active account
paths.description: Adoption healthy from day 30, positive renewal signal at 90-day QBR

paths.name: Low adoption — intervention required
paths.description: Adoption concerns at 30 days trigger CS intervention before 60-day check-in

paths.name: At-risk account — renewal intervention
paths.description: Red renewal signal at 90-day QBR triggers escalated intervention

phases.name: Account Setup
phases.goal: Establish CRM record and prepare for client kick-off

phases.name: Kick-off and Stakeholder Mapping
phases.goal: Establish relationship and identify key contacts

phases.name: Implementation Support
phases.goal: Support successful implementation and monitor adoption

phases.name: Value Realisation
phases.goal: Confirm client is achieving intended business outcomes

phases.name: Ongoing Management
phases.goal: Sustain relationship health and manage renewal

researchSources.source: B2B sales onboarding and CRM process research, Salesforce best practice documentation
Composite from senior sales representative research (Maria Rodriguez actor development)
